confirmed: Read the complete on-file markdown through its final reference and checked relevant PDF text, Table 1 via find_tables(), and Figures 1 and 8 visually; the PDF is the 16-page Frontiers in Psychology journal article published 17 June 2026 (p. 1; references end p. 16). The separate online supplement was not read.

One original people experiment, not a synthesis or AI-versus-human-output comparison; field_rct and context_class=none are supported by random assignment within a university course (pp. 3–4, Sections 3.1–3.2).

Random assignment is explicitly of students after class sampling, followed by reorganization into mixed-class groups and independent task completion; the authors’ quasi-experimental label does not negate that stated mechanism (pp. 3–4, Sections 3.1–3.2).

The total of 120 assigned students and 120 analyzed people is supported by Section 3.2, the starting groups in Figure 8, and N=40 per arm in Table 1; these are students, not ideas or ratings, and the study is above the 50-person threshold (p. 4; p. 9). No exclusions or attrition are stated in the article.
The participant quote’s ages 19–22 years, M=20.4 and SD=0.84 match the PDF (p. 4, Section 3.2).
Both AI groups used Deepseek and Dreamina, with the Double Diamond operation sheet only in GAI-SDTS; TDL used conventional resources and design tools such as Photoshop (p. 5, Section 3.3).
The form correctly describes a four-week design course, preparation in Week 1, design production in Weeks 2–5, and assessment in Week 6 (p. 4, Section 3.2; pp. 8–9, Section 3.5 and Figure 8).

The output outcome is composite design achievement rated by instructors, explicitly including Creativity; creative self-efficacy and perceived problem-solving are questionnaire measures, not additional scored-output creativity outcomes (p. 8, Section 3.4; p. 9, Section 3.5).
The existing reported string exactly matches Table 1: GAI N=40, Mean=18.65, S.D.=7.41; TDL N=40, Mean=16.13, S.D.=6.85; Section 4.1 explicitly reports Tukey GAI>TDL, p<0.001 (p. 9).

The one-line finding’s means 20.90, 18.65, and 16.13, total sample of 120, and statement that all Tukey pairwise comparisons were reported as p<0.001 match the source; these are composite design-achievement scores, not separate creativity scores (p. 4, Section 3.2; p. 9, Table 1 and Section 4.1).

No separate creativity-component estimate, between-person diversity outcome, later unassisted creativity task, or pooled synthesis estimate is reported in the main article (pp. 8–11, Sections 3.4–4.3 and Tables 1–3; p. 13, Section 5.6).

The supplement description is supported only to the stated extent: Supplementary Table S1 contains the DDDOS, and supplementary material is linked separately rather than included in this PDF (p. 5, Section 3.3; p. 14, Supplementary material).

The article declares no financial support and no commercial or financial conflicts; raw data are to be made available by the authors, without a deposited data or code URL in the statement (p. 14, Funding, Conflict of interest, and Data availability statement).
summary: Random assignment of 120 students and artwork scoring that includes creativity support referral to the two-screener pipeline. Recorded statistics match the PDF; corrections address allocation counts, incomplete fields, and eligibility coding.
